conventions.convention: The Euclidean SU(2) action is an independent adopted classical model, not derived from the Lorentzian postulate. The base is closed and oriented; the R4 alternative requires specified smooth S4 extension data in addition to finite action.
Generators are anti-Hermitian, T_a = −iσ_a/2, with tr(T_a T_b) = −δ_ab/2. The action uses κ = −2tr, while the charge uses B_top = −tr = κ/2.

With full AC and the supplied characteristic-class comparison, ν = −(8π²)⁻¹∫tr(F∧F) = −⟨c₂(E),[X]⟩ is integral. Positive-charge instantons are self-dual; negative-charge anti-instantons are anti-self-dual. Instanton saddles must have nonzero charge.

Bundle sectors use the supplied minimum-rank set codes, with a model-specified set of admitted sectors and supplied representative bundles. The integer charge is not claimed to classify all components or gauge orbits.
The sector expression uses e^{iθν} and is formal notation only: no functional measure, gauge fixing, determinant, convergence, or continuum quantum construction is supplied.
The BPST sphere is oriented positively in north stereographic coordinates, and right-action local sections satisfy s_S = s_N u⁻¹, hence A_S = Ad_u A_N + u d(u⁻¹).

load_bearing.statement: Adopt, independently of any Lorentzian theory, the source-free pure Euclidean SU(2) model on exactly these supplied geometric data. No matter fields are present. For dimensionless g_YM > 0, adopt S_E[A] = (2g_YM²)⁻¹∫_M κ(F_A∧*F_A).

A classical Euclidean saddle is a smooth admissible connection whose first variation of S_E vanishes for every smooth compactly supported connection variation preserving the boundary data. An instanton (respectively anti-instanton) saddle is a nonzero-charge saddle satisfying the positive (respectively negative) self-duality equation.
Assuming full AC, on the specified nonempty connected closed oriented Riemannian four-manifold, q_B is connection-independent. For defining-representation SU(2) and B = −tr₂, q_B = −⟨c₂(E),[X]⟩ ∈ Z.
Assuming full AC, the explicitly specified two-chart connection on the oriented round S4 is smooth and self-dual, has q_B = 1 for B = −tr₂, and has S_B(g) = 8π²/g² for every real g > 0.

Under its full-AC, closed oriented Riemannian four-manifold, supplied connection, and invariant positive-definite B hypotheses, S_B ≥ 8π²|q_B|/g². Every self-dual or anti-self-dual supplied connection satisfies D_A(*F_A) = 0.

published_dependencies.used_for: The explicit countable-choice assumption inherited by the gauge-data and connection constructions.
Full-choice hypotheses of the integral charge comparison and both examples.
Gauge transformations as smooth equivariant bundle automorphisms covering the identity.
The BPST example's first-variation integration by parts on closed S4; compact support and countable choice are satisfied.
Indirect supplier for the smooth right principal-bundle conventions and two-chart gluing construction.
Indirect supplier for the SU(2) matrix Lie-group structure and traceless skew-Hermitian Lie algebra.
Indirect supplier for compactness of SU(2) as a closed bounded subset of R8.
Indirect charge supplier fixing c(∇) = det(I − Ω/(2πi)); its rank-two expansion gives the stated negative c2 charge convention.
Indirect charge supplier identifying Hermitian Chern forms with realifications of integral Chern classes under full AC.

concerns.concern: The observable paragraph requires O to be constant on connection data 'related by a smooth diffeomorphism Φ:P→P' satisfying the gauge-automorphism conditions, but never defines the relation on connections. State explicitly the pullback action, for example O(s,Φ*ω)=O(s,ω) whenever both configurations are admissible, and specify preservation of the supplied extension/boundary data in the flat branch. The cited gauge-group definition defines the automorphisms, not this action.

Verification 2.2 ends 'proving the saddle condition in [A1]'. A1 states full AC; A2 contains the saddle definition. The calculation establishes the intended condition, but the prose points to the wrong assumption.

seams_checked.note: The SU(2) invariant-form lemma supplies precisely the stated normalization. The Lorentzian postulate has only a Minkowski branch; the consumer correctly introduces an independent Euclidean postulate rather than claiming Wick rotation follows from it.

The charge uses B_top = −tr₂, retains the negative c2 sign and full-AC qualification, and uses the supplied compactified connection. It does not strengthen charge labels into a classification of all components or gauge orbits.

The consumer preserves right principal actions, reproduction and equivariance of connection forms, the half-bracket curvature normalization, minimum-rank sector coding, and the local curvature transition law.

The BPST example reproduces the supplier's charts, orientation, transition and potentials. Its ν=1 and action follow with κ=2B_top. The action-bound supplier gives the Bianchi consequence; the example separately proves stationarity by Stokes. The vacuum example correctly excludes zero charge from the instanton definition.
